subject: Defining acceptance: success assertions, exit tests, and failover plan

Hi Lauren — thanks, and glad the demo resonated. I've sketched a concise acceptance plan below and attached a working MAP and a CSV with example test vignettes. This is intentionally lightweight so procurement has what it needs and engineering can start running tests immediately.

High-level acceptance summary (30-day pilot):
- Success assertions (must all be true to recommend commit):
  1) Mean 95th-pct token latency <= 220ms on your median request distribution (as measured by Redwood tracing agent).
  2) End-to-end throughput supports your peak concurrency pattern with <=5% request drop or queuing at target reserved capacity.
  3) Semantic accuracy: top-1 answer precision >= 88% on the provided label set (sample of 500).
  4) No critical security or data handling discrepancy per our shared SOC2 checklist.

- Exit gates (immediate stop / extension triggers):
  * Immediate stop: model returns PHI/PII leakage beyond agreed redaction rules OR service-level incident > 1 hour causing >25% errors.
  * Soft stop / extension: accuracy below threshold but improving after 7 days of tuning OR performance regressions that require infra tuning (we propose a 7-day remediation window).

- Acceptance test suite (smoke -> integration):
  1) Smoke: end-to-end generation on 50 seed prompts, verify run completes and latency recorded.
  2) Accuracy vignettes: 500 labeled prompts (attached CSV); compute top-1 precision and a small confusion breakdown.
  3) Load ramp: 1, 5, 10 concurrent simulated clients (30 min each) to observe queueing and scaling behavior.
  4) Failover simulation: introduce 20% pod loss to validate routing/fallback to compatible model variant.
  5) Data isolation probe: sample request logs to confirm no cross-tenant cache leakage.

- Evidence checklist for procurement/security:
  - SOC2 Type II summary + point of contact for full report (we can provide redacted).
  - Data retention and deletion playbook (how KV/prefix caches are handled).
  - Audit log sample (tracing per-request breadcrumbs for 1 day).
  - Infra network diagram for Private/Dedicated options.

Owners & timeline:
- Redwood lead: Soojin Lee (pilot plan & run coordination)
- Technical validation: Ben Carter (performance & failover tests), Karthik Iyer (accuracy & model config)
- Procurement liaison: Monica Patel (contracts & evidence)

Next steps (for your Tuesday deadline):
1) Confirm the two technical validators at BrightPath (we suggested Aaron + one SWE).
2) Approve the attached acceptance CSV and MAP-v0.2.xlsx.
3) We'll run the smoke tests within 48 hours of receiving the sample corpus and share a first report.

I'll loop Ben & Karthik below with a short note on the test vignettes and remediation plan.

Thanks —
Sooj in

Following up with the technical acceptance vignettes and the failover/playback steps — tagging the precise checks we'll run and what evidence we will deliver. Quoting Soojin's list below.

Technical acceptance checklist (deltas / concrete tests):
- Latency: collect 95th percentile per-token and per-request across 24h. Deliverable: CSV timeline + flamegraph of hot calls. Threshold: 95th <= 220ms.
- Throughput: synthetic ramp with load-generator; watch queue depth and per-request tail latency. Deliverable: load-run artifact + autoscaler events.
- Accuracy: run your labeled 500 set in A/B vs our tuned quantized variant; deliverable: confusion matrix + 10 representative failures with model output and expected label.
- Failover: induce pod removal (k8s drain) on 2/10 serving nodes and verify request continuity via smart routing. Deliverable: timeline showing no more than 1-minute spike in error rate and automated fallback logs.
- Security probes: automated query with known-PII triggers; ensure redaction and log-only flagged events. Deliverable: redaction report + sample audit log entries.

Remediation ladder (if a gate fails):
1) Day 0 — Triage (owner assigned, hotfix attempt).
2) Day 1–3 — Config tuning (kernel selection, quantization bump, batch size changes).
3) Day 4–7 — If still failing, propose extension window and rolling canary with a narrower traffic slice.

Evidence package we will upload to the shared Drive link (read-only to BrightPath procurement):
- acceptance_report_{date}.zip (includes CSVs, flamegraphs, runbooks)
- audit_snippets.json (sample, redacted)
- runbook_summary.md (what we changed and why)

I'll start the load runs as soon as we have the sample corpus and your confirmation on the validation contacts.

—Ben
